title: Firestore - NOT_FOUND read volume day-over-day step

annotations.summary: Firestore document read_count (metric stackdriver_firestore_instance_firestore_googleapis_com_document_read_count, type="NOT_FOUND") is running more than 2x its volume from the same hour yesterday, sustained for 2h.
annotations.threshold: avg_over_time(avg(...)[1h:1m]) > 2x the same expression offset 24h, sustained 2h
annotations.user_impact: No direct user impact; this is a cost signal, not an outage. NOT_FOUND reads are Firestore reads for documents that do not exist, so they are near-pure waste: the read is billed but returns nothing. The day-over-day comparison survives organic growth and diurnal swing, so a sustained step here is a regression rather than load.
annotations.scope: Firestore document reads across the based-hardware production project, type="NOT_FOUND" only.
annotations.verification: Compare avg_over_time(avg(stackdriver_firestore_instance_firestore_googleapis_com_document_read_count{type="NOT_FOUND"})[1h:1m]) against the same expression with `offset 24h`. The 2x factor is measured, not guessed: across 2026-08-18..25 excluding the incident window, normal day-over-day ratios peaked at 1.94x for a single hour, while the 2026-08-23 step held 2.4-3.4x for 24h straight. A 1.5x threshold would have false-positived on 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-21. The stackdriver exporter publishes this DELTA metric as a GAUGE whose value is the per-60s-window count, so rate() is meaningless on it -- read volume must be recovered with avg_over_time(...)/60 instead. avg() (not sum()) aggregates across exporter replicas, which all report the same Cloud Monitoring series.
annotations.safe_next_action: This alert flags read volume, not cause. The Cloud Monitoring series carries module="__unknown__", so attribution needs either extending omi_firestore_read_operations_total call-site coverage or enabling a short window of Firestore DATA_READ audit logging to find the caller before making any code change.

title: Firestore - NOT_FOUND read volume above absolute ceiling

annotations.summary: Firestore document read_count (metric stackdriver_firestore_instance_firestore_googleapis_com_document_read_count, type="NOT_FOUND") has averaged more than 750 reads/sec over a rolling 6h window. Measured separation over 2026-08-18..25: the highest pre-incident 6h mean was 668/sec and the lowest post-incident 6h mean was 899/sec, so this threshold sits in a clean gap with ~12% margin on each side.
annotations.user_impact: No direct user impact; this is a cost signal, not an outage. NOT_FOUND reads are Firestore reads for documents that do not exist, so they are near-pure waste: the read is billed but returns nothing. At the 2026-08-23 incident rate of ~950/sec this class of read alone costs roughly $740/month. This is the backstop for a leak already running at a steady elevated rate, which the day-over-day step detector cannot see because both sides of its comparison are equally elevated.
annotations.scope: Firestore document reads across the based-hardware production project, type="NOT_FOUND" only.
annotations.verification: Run avg_over_time(avg(stackdriver_firestore_instance_firestore_googleapis_com_document_read_count{type="NOT_FOUND"})[6h:5m]) / 60 in the linked query. Healthy 6h means run 347-668/sec; the 2026-08-23 leak holds 899-1049/sec. A 6h window is used deliberately: hourly values are extremely spiky (single healthy hours reach 1124/sec), so any shorter window false-positives. The stackdriver exporter publishes this DELTA metric as a GAUGE whose value is the per-60s-window count, so rate() is meaningless on it -- read volume must be recovered with avg_over_time(...)/60 instead. avg() (not sum()) aggregates across exporter replicas, which all report the same Cloud Monitoring series.
annotations.safe_next_action: This alert flags read volume, not cause. The Cloud Monitoring series carries module="__unknown__", so attribution needs either extending omi_firestore_read_operations_total call-site coverage or enabling a short window of Firestore DATA_READ audit logging to find the caller before making any code change.

title: Firestore - read-volume metric stopped being collected

annotations.summary: The Firestore read-volume series (stackdriver_firestore_instance_firestore_googleapis_com_document_read_count, type="NOT_FOUND") has been absent from Prometheus for 30m, so both Firestore cost alerts are blind.
annotations.user_impact: No direct user impact. This is a watchdog for the cost alerts themselves. Both Firestore cost rules are written as `expr > threshold`, which returns an empty vector when not firing; with noDataState=OK, a metric that stops arriving is indistinguishable from a healthy one. This rule is what makes that difference visible.
annotations.scope: The stackdriver-exporter series for firestore.googleapis.com/document/read_count in prod Prometheus.
annotations.verification: Query stackdriver_firestore_instance_firestore_googleapis_com_document_read_count in the linked datasource. Expect 3 series (type=LOOKUP|NOT_FOUND|QUERY). Zero series means the exporter is not publishing.
annotations.safe_next_action: This has a known cause with a known fix. Check the exporter pod for scrape errors: at monitoring.descriptor-cache-ttl=0s the exporter re-runs ListMetricDescriptors every scrape and Cloud Monitoring answers with 503 cpu-protection, which drops all series. Also check that stackdriver.metrics.interval still exceeds the ~2.4min Firestore ingestion lag -- a window shorter than the lag is always empty and yields no series at all. Both settings live in backend/charts/monitoring/prometheus-stackdriver-exporter/prod_omi_stackdriver_exporter.yaml and are applied manually per that chart README; no workflow deploys them.

title: Firestore - projected read spend per day above ceiling

annotations.summary: Projected Firestore document-read spend has exceeded $500/day on a 6h rolling mean. Measured baseline on 2026-08-25 was $344-368/day (~14,200 reads/sec), so this is ~40% headroom.
annotations.user_impact: No direct user impact; this is the money rule. Unlike the NOT_FOUND rules it is shape-agnostic -- it catches a regression in LOOKUP, QUERY, or NOT_FOUND reads, from application code OR from a Firebase Extension, which the app-side probe cannot see. On 2026-08-25 QUERY reads were ~13,000/sec against NOT_FOUND ~920/sec, so a NOT_FOUND-only alert watches ~7% of the bill.
annotations.verification: Run the expression in the linked datasource. The $0.03/100k rate is an ASSUMPTION, not a verified Omi contract price -- re-derive from the billing export before quoting the dollar figure. The ratio and the trend are the durable signal.
annotations.safe_next_action: Break down by family with sum by (family) (rate(omi_firestore_documents_per_operation_sum[1h])). On 2026-08-25 action_items_list alone was 5,079 reads/sec, ~36% of all Firestore read spend. See omi-knowledge-base/projects/gcp-cost-efficiency/candidates/C006-action-items-list-polling.md. Thresholds are measured, not guessed, and each expression was proven to return a series at a lowered threshold and nothing at its real one before shipping -- see FC-alert-never-provably-fired. stackdriver_* series are DELTA published as GAUGES (per-60s counts), so rate() on them is meaningless; omi_* _total series are real counters and rate() is correct.

title: Firestore - a read family doubled day-over-day

model.expr: (sum by (family) (rate(omi_firestore_documents_per_operation_sum[2h])) > 2 * sum by (family) (rate(omi_firestore_documents_per_operation_sum[2h] offset 24h))) and (sum by (family) (rate(omi_firestore_documents_per_operation_sum[2h])) > 100)

annotations.summary: An instrumented Firestore read family is reading more than 2x the documents per second it read at the same time yesterday, and is above 100 docs/sec in absolute terms.
annotations.threshold: per-family rate > 2x the same rate offset 24h, AND > 100 docs/sec, sustained 1h
annotations.user_impact: No direct user impact; cost signal. This is the rule that names WHICH read path regressed -- the platform metric cannot, because all 31 firestore.googleapis.com descriptors lack any collection dimension. The 100 docs/sec floor stops small families from flapping; the 2x factor matches the measured day-over-day envelope (normal peaks reached 1.94x over 2026-08-18..25).
annotations.scope: Families instrumented via omi_firestore_read_operations_total / omi_firestore_documents_per_operation. Coverage is partial by design; a path with no family label is invisible here.

Note that "bounded" in FirestoreReadMode means a bound was applied, NOT that a cache exists -- action_items_list is bounded at limit=500 and still reads ~5,000 docs/sec because every client poll re-reads the list. annotations.summary: Firestore Commit calls are returning RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED at more than 10 per minute for 5 consecutive minutes
annotations.user_impact: Contended or throttled commits expire in-flight transactions (batch retention, cap persist); work retries or is lost until the hotspot clears.
annotations.scope: Cloud Monitoring firestore.googleapis.com/api/request_count for the based-hardware default database, Commit only. Hotspot evidence: KB projects/two-lane-transcription/evidence/2026-10-21-firestore-hotspots-key-visualizer.md.
annotations.verification: Backtest 2026-10-14..10-21 (Cloud Monitoring, 60s ALIGN_DELTA): RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED on Commit was nonzero in 958 minutes (60.7k total; nonzero-minute p50 9, p90 147, max 2,351). Sustained episodes: > 0 for 2m = 217 in 7d (too noisy to page on); > 10/min for 5m = 18 (latest 10-20 16:16Z, 18:02Z, 18:32Z); > 50/min for 5m = 8; > 10/min for 10m = 5.
annotations.safe_next_action: Open the Firestore Key Visualizer for the hot key range and match it to the batch retention / cap-persist writers before changing write rates.

title: Firestore - caller label set overflowed into other

annotations.summary: The Firestore read caller label set has overflowed into other: a new call site is no longer named, so by-caller attribution is silently folding.
annotations.user_impact: No direct user impact; this is an attribution and cost-visibility signal. Reads keep being served, but a new or changed read path stops being named in the by-caller counter, so a read regression on it can no longer be attributed to a call site.
annotations.scope: omi_firestore_billed_reads_by_caller_total{caller="other"} and omi_firestore_caller_label_overflow_total from the Python Firestore read probe (backend/database/firestore_document_probe.py), queried on the managed gmp-cloud-run datasource so Cloud Run and GKE are both covered. The cap is MAX_CALLERS (1536) distinct module:function labels per process.
annotations.verification: Run sum(rate(omi_firestore_billed_reads_by_caller_total{caller="other"}[5m])) and sum(rate(omi_firestore_caller_label_overflow_total[5m])) on gmp-cloud-run. A non-zero overflow rate means a well-formed new caller arrived after the cap filled; a non-zero other read rate without overflow means a malformed or frame-less caller label. Both are folding. Confirm the probe image is current before changing the cap. An empty result on both arms is the expected healthy state, because the caller=other bucket only exists after a fold; report it as "no series" and never as a measured clean zero.
annotations.safe_next_action: Identify the folded call site from the deploy that started serving just before the first overflow, then either raise MAX_CALLERS in a reviewed PR with the measured function count, or fix the malformed label. Never add a uid, document id or query text as a label. Kill switch: set node D (vector(1)) to vector(0) and re-provision; restore vector(1) to re-enable. The rule also ships isPaused=false; pausing it is the operational switch.
annotations.threshold: sum(rate(omi_firestore_billed_reads_by_caller_total{caller="other"}[5m])) > 0 OR sum(rate(omi_firestore_caller_label_overflow_total[5m])) > 0, sustained 5m, gated by the enable selector node D vector(1).
annotations.evaluated_bad: Fixture, not a live backtest: the counter is new in this program and no production overflow window exists yet. With MAX_CALLERS=1 a second well-formed caller folds to other and omi_firestore_caller_label_overflow_total increments by 1; the rule evaluates to 1. See backend/tests/unit/test_firestore_caller_overflow_alert.py.
annotations.evaluated_good: Fixture: with the caller set not full, bound_caller returns the named label, the overflow counter does not move, and the rule evaluates to 0. Same test file.
annotations.kill_switch: Enable selector node D vector(1) in this rule, enabled by default. Disable: set node D to vector(0) and run python3 backend/scripts/provision_monitoring_alerts.py --apply. Re-enable: restore vector(1) and re-provision. Operational switch: isPaused (ships false). No actuator flips either automatically.

title: Firestore - unattributed reads above 3% of billed reads

annotations.summary: Unattributed Firestore reads are above 3% of billed reads on a 30m window: the instrumented read counters cover less than 97% of the native document/read_count.
annotations.threshold: ($B - $A) / $B > 0.03 for 30m, where A = sum(rate(omi_firestore_billed_reads_by_caller_total[30m])) or vector(0), B = avg_over_time(sum(firestore_googleapis_com:document_read_count)[30m:1m]) / 60, and the same 30m window is used on both sides. The rule resolves at or below 0.03. The denominator's completeness and per-type freshness are guarded independently by omi-firestore-unattributed-reads-blind.
annotations.user_impact: No direct user impact. A blind spot in read attribution means a read regression can grow without a named caller, so the next cost cut cannot be proven and the bill can rise unseen.
annotations.scope: based-hardware, both Firestore databases, all read types (LOOKUP, QUERY, NOT_FOUND). A is the complete instrumented counter on the GMP datasource (Cloud Run and GKE); B is the native Cloud Monitoring document/read_count, which tracked the settled bill to 0.3% on the 2026-11-09 cross-check. A missing instrumented series reads as zero through or vector(0) and fires. The separate guard rule fires when the billed series is incomplete, stale or absent, so this rule's NoData is covered.
annotations.verification: Exact expression replayed on GMP query_range 2026-11-02T06:51Z..2026-11-12T06:51Z at 1h steps (241 points): 0.134-0.568, mean 0.321. Daily means: 11-09 0.274, 11-10 0.196, 11-11 0.163, 11-12 0.162. No retained hour is at or below 0.03, so the resolve side is proven by fixtures, not by live history. The 95% acceptance figure in backend/docs/firestore-read-attribution.md is historical; the fresh measurement is 84% attributed.
annotations.evaluated_good: Fixture: instrumented 980/s against billed 1000/s (gap 0.02) for 2h produces no episode, and a firing episode resolves on the first chronological tick at exactly 0.03.
annotations.safe_next_action: Read the by-caller coverage per kind on the Firestore dashboard, then confirm the instrumented fleet is on a probe build that exports by_caller. If omi-firestore-unattributed-reads-blind is firing, fix the billed series before reading this ratio. This rule reports the gap; it does not explain it, and the closed QUERY undercount RCA is not reopened here.
annotations.switch: isPaused=false (enabled by default). Disable: set isPaused true and re-import; re-enable: set isPaused false. Selector: membership of this UID in backend/charts/monitoring/live-alert-gate.json uids[] controls fail-closed live import and verification; it is present by default and is listed in PRODUCTION_ONLY_IMPORT_UIDS because the gmp-cloud-run datasource exists only in production. The guard rule has its own isPaused switch and its own gate UID.

title: Firestore - unattributed-reads guard: billed series incomplete or stale

model.expr: ((count(count by (type) (firestore_googleapis_com:document_read_count{type=~"LOOKUP|QUERY|NOT_FOUND"})) == bool 3) or vector(0)) * ((min((max by (type) (time() - timestamp(firestore_googleapis_com:document_read_count{type=~"LOOKUP|QUERY|NOT_FOUND"}))) < bool 900)) or vector(0))

annotations.summary: The billed Firestore read series is incomplete, stale or absent, so the unattributed-reads ratio is blind.
annotations.threshold: A < 1 for 30m, where A = (count of LOOKUP|QUERY|NOT_FOUND == 3) * (min per expected type of (max by type (time() - timestamp(...)) < 900)); the selectors name LOOKUP, QUERY and NOT_FOUND explicitly, so an unknown type cannot replace an expected type. NoData is Alerting.
annotations.user_impact: No direct user impact. A blind denominator means the unattributed-reads alert cannot tell a real attribution gap from a vanished or stale billed series, so a read regression could pass unmeasured.
annotations.scope: based-hardware, the three expected billed types (LOOKUP, QUERY, NOT_FOUND) on the gmp-cloud-run datasource. The guard is 1 only when all three expected types are present and every expected type is younger than 900s. An unknown type is excluded from both the count and the freshness check, so it cannot replace a missing expected type. Partial type loss, one stale type, total loss and a missing metric all drive the guard to 0; NoData is Alerting as a final fail-closed layer.
annotations.verification: Measured 2026-11-13T10:39Z on GMP: count by type = 3, max age 143s, guard = 1. Fixtures exercise all three expected types fresh (guard 1), one stale type with two fresh (guard 0), an absent series (guard 0), and each of LOOKUP/QUERY/NOT_FOUND replaced by a fresh unknown type (guard 0).
annotations.evaluated_bad: Fixture: LOOKUP 100s, QUERY 2000s, NOT_FOUND 100s -> guard 0 -> fires. Absent metric -> guard 0 -> fires. Each expected type replaced by FUTURE_TYPE at 100s -> guard 0 -> fires (unknown types cannot substitute). NoData is Alerting.
annotations.evaluated_good: Fixture: all three types at 100s -> guard 1 -> no episode.
annotations.safe_next_action: Check the GMP series for a missing type or a stale sample before reading the ratio. Do not treat the ratio's NoData as healthy.
annotations.switch: isPaused=false (enabled by default). Disable: set isPaused true and re-import; re-enable: set isPaused false. Selector: membership of this UID in backend/charts/monitoring/live-alert-gate.json uids[] controls fail-closed live import and verification; it is present by default and is listed in PRODUCTION_ONLY_IMPORT_UIDS because the gmp-cloud-run datasource exists only in production.

annotations.summary: Last full UTC hour of billed reads exceeds 1.25x the median of the same hour on the previous seven days. Incomplete current/history coverage or a zero median is an agent-tier telemetry ticket.
annotations.threshold: Last full UTC hour of billed reads exceeds 1.25x the median of the same hour on the previous seven days. Incomplete current/history coverage or a zero median is an agent-tier telemetry ticket. Sustained for 2h.
annotations.user_impact: Cost regression only; no direct user outage. Ticket, not a page.
annotations.scope: Production fleet on gmp-cloud-run; Cloud Run and GKE. Native billed reads include all read types and both databases.
annotations.verification: Compare sum by (caller) (increase(omi_firestore_billed_reads_by_caller_total[1h])) with the same query offset 1d. GMP live evaluation is required before release; fixtures are not production measurements.
annotations.evaluated_bad: Fixture: 126M reads against a 100M same-hour median fires.
annotations.evaluated_good: Fixture: Exactly 1.25x or less does not fire; one daily outlier does not move the median.
annotations.safe_next_action: Firestore cost owner (SCA-2173): compare caller reads against the same hour yesterday. If NoData, require all three native read types and at least 58 raw minute samples per series in the current hour and each of seven baseline hours, plus a positive median, before interpreting the step. Do not change runtime settings from this alert alone.
annotations.switch: Enabled by default: isPaused=false; disable with isPaused=true and re-import. Keep ticket severity until the ratio has been below the 45,000 budget once; promotion requires an explicit follow-up change.
